notes.meaning: All people on earth are invited to praise the Lord with a fresh song. This new song celebrates God's wonderful rescue through Christ, which is always fresh and never fades away. It shows that God's grace reaches beyond one nation to the whole world.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars connect this call for a new song to Isaiah 42:10, celebrating God's mercy in bringing Israel home from exile in Babylon.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine taught that the old song belongs to selfish human desires, while the new song belongs to Christ's new command of love lived out in the worldwide church.

notes.meaning: God's people are told to bless His name and announce His salvation day after day. Salvation means God's rescue of sinners from danger and death. Sharing this good news should be a daily joy that never stops.

Worshipers must tell all nations about the Lord's greatness and the amazing miracles He has done. The message of what God has done in Christ is meant for every people group on earth. Believers are called to spread His fame everywhere.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine applied this to preaching God's honor rather than one's own, and urged unity with the whole church spread across all nations.

notes.meaning: The Lord is truly great and deserves more praise than anyone else. He is not a small, local ruler, but the master over all powers. Proper reverence and holy awe belong to Him alone.

The gods that other nations worship are mere idols, which are empty nothings with no life at all. In contrast, the Lord made the heavens and the stars above. The Creator alone has the right to be worshiped.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Following an ancient Greek translation, Augustine taught that the false gods of the nations are actually demons.

notes.meaning: Royal honor and majesty surround the Lord wherever He is. Strength and beauty fill His holy dwelling place. In God, great power and lovely goodness come together for His people to enjoy.

Families from every nation are summoned to give the Lord glory and strength. Giving Him glory does not add anything new to Him, but simply honors what is already true of Him. No race or tribe is left out of this call.

All people are told to give the Lord the honor His name is owed and to enter His courts with an offering. This offering is a gift of thanks and willing submission to the true King. True worship includes giving our best back to God.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine explained that the true offering to bring into God's presence is a humble and repentant heart.

notes.meaning: People are commanded to bow down before the Lord in the beauty of holiness and tremble in His presence. God values pure hearts and sincere lives far more than outward show or fine buildings. Deep reverence is the right response before a holy God.

The nations must hear the good news that the Lord reigns as King over all. His righteous rule makes the world secure against chaos and brings true stability to human society. He governs all peoples with fairness and truth.

differ.view: Many evangelicals believe this reign began through Christ's first coming and the spread of the gospel in the hearts of believers.
Some evangelicals believe this reign refers specifically to Christ's future rule on earth during an earthly kingdom after His return.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early church writers noted an old reading that said the Lord reigns from the wood, meaning that Christ reigns as King through His cross.

notes.meaning: The heavens, the earth, and the roaring sea are called to burst into gladness. The open fields and the trees of the forest join in the celebration as well. Creation rejoices because God's good rule will set the world free from the damage of sin.

All creation sings because the Lord is coming to judge and rule the earth. His judging is not cruel, but a fair and faithful leadership that rights every wrong. Believers can look forward to His righteous reign with great hope.

differ.view: Many evangelicals believe this describes Christ ruling by the gospel now and finishing that work at the final day of judgment.
Some evangelicals believe this points to Christ's bodily return to earth to judge nations and establish His earthly kingdom.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Ancient Christian teachers saw the repeated phrase that He is coming as pointing first to Christ's birth as a man and second to His coming to judge the world.
